text: Welcome to Miami, baby. I got you. What's the vibe — beach day, eating your way through the city, big night out, culture crawl, or something with the family? Just say the word.

Miami eats different — literally. What are you feeling? Cuban comfort food at Versailles on Calle Ocho is the move for a first-timer. Want upscale? Cote in the Design District is Michelin-starred Korean steakhouse that'll change your life. Seafood? Joe's Stone Crab if you're here before May — get in the takeout line, skip the 2-hour wait.

Little Havana is the soul of Miami. Start at Versailles — order the vaca frita and a cafecito at the ventanita. Walk down to Ball & Chain for live salsa. Azucar Ice Cream for dessert — get the Abuela Maria flavor. Then hit El Palacio de los Jugos for the real-deal roast pork. This is not tourist Miami — this is Miami Miami.

For the big night: Cote Miami for Korean steakhouse perfection. The Surf Club by Thomas Keller in Surfside is Continental elegance with a Michelin star. Los Fuegos at the Faena is Francis Mallmann's live-fire temple — the most romantic restaurant in Miami. And Zucca in Coral Gables does refined Italian with a 2,000-bottle wine cellar.
businesses: The Surf Club Restaurant by Thomas Keller

text: You can eat like a king in Miami for $15. El Palacio de los Jugos — point at the roast pork, get yuca and a mamey shake. Caracas Bakery on Biscayne for a ham cachito that'll make you cry. Cotoletta in the Design District — one perfect Milanese cutlet, that's the whole menu, and it's worth every penny.

Miami nightlife doesn't even start until midnight — plan accordingly. LIV at Fontainebleau is THE mega-club. E11EVEN is the 24/7 ultraclub that doesn't close, ever. Club Space is where the real house/techno heads go — the Sunday morning terrace set at sunrise is a Miami rite of passage. Want something less intense? Sweet Liberty is the best cocktail bar on the Beach.

Sweet Liberty on Collins is award-winning — just tell the bartender what you're in the mood for. The Broken Shaker at the Freehand is craft cocktails by a pool. Sugar at EAST Miami is the rooftop move — go at sunset. And if you want zero pretension, Mac's Club Deuce is a 1964 dive bar where beers are cheap and nobody cares what you're wearing.

Ball & Chain on Calle Ocho for live salsa — Salsero Sundays are iconic. Mango's on Ocean Drive is the over-the-top spectacle with dancers and piña coladas in pineapples. Hoy Como Ayer in Little Havana for a more local vibe. And El Patio in Wynwood is reggaeton central on Fridays.

South Beach at Lummus Park is the scene — lifeguard towers, beautiful people, Ocean Drive right behind you. But locals go to Crandon Park on Key Biscayne for calmer water and real relaxation. South Pointe Park at the tip of the Beach is my favorite spot — watch cruise ships glide by. Haulover Beach is gorgeous too (heads up: the north end is clothing-optional).

Take an airboat through the Everglades — gators, roseate spoonbills, the whole River of Grass, 45 min from downtown. Oleta River State Park has mountain biking and mangrove kayaking inside the city. Biscayne National Park is 95% underwater — snorkeling on the third-largest barrier reef in the world. Fairchild Tropical Garden is a quiet masterpiece on the Bay.

Design District for luxury — Gucci, Dior, Louis Vuitton, plus the architecture is incredible. Lincoln Road on the Beach for a pedestrian mall vibe with outdoor dining. Dolphin Mall if you want outlet deals. And the Sunday farmer's market on Lincoln Road is great for local stuff.

This is a cafecito city. Any ventanita (walk-up window) on Calle Ocho serves Cuban coffee for $1 that'll rewire your nervous system. For specialty, Panther Coffee in Wynwood roasts their own. Caracas Bakery on Biscayne does Venezuelan pastries and great coffee together.

South Beach for nightlife and scene: Fontainebleau is the icon, Faena is the art hotel, 1 Hotel is eco-luxury. Brickell for a modern, urban base close to restaurants and rooftop bars. Freehand is the best budget play — boutique hostel with the Broken Shaker bar. Coral Gables for a quieter, residential feel.

MIA is the main airport — global hub, direct flights everywhere. FLL (Fort Lauderdale) is 30 min north and often way cheaper. Brightline train connects MIA to Fort Lauderdale in 30 min and Orlando in 3.5 hours. Once here? Uber everywhere, or grab the free Metromover downtown. The free trolley runs through Wynwood, Brickell, and Little Havana. Parking on the Beach is expensive — valet or take a ride.

text: Frost Museum of Science has a 3-story aquarium and planetarium — kids lose their minds. Zoo Miami is the only tropical zoo in the continental US. Jungle Island has ziplines and animal encounters. Crandon Park Beach on Key Biscayne has calm water perfect for little ones. And the free Metromover is basically an amusement ride for toddlers.
businesses: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science

text: Sunset dinner at Los Fuegos at the Faena — fire-grilled Argentine perfection in the most beautiful hotel in Miami. Walk the Vizcaya gardens at golden hour. Cocktails on the rooftop at Sugar in Brickell. Then close the night at Sweet Liberty. If you really want to go all out, a private sunset cruise on Biscayne Bay — the skyline at dusk is unmatched.

Your perfect Miami day: Cafecito at a ventanita to start. Walk the Art Deco District to South Pointe Park. Lunch at Gramps Getaway on the marina. Afternoon at Crandon Park Beach. Shower and change — dinner at Tropezón on Española Way. Then cocktails at Sweet Liberty, and finish at LIV or Ball & Chain depending on your vibe.

Miami always has something going on. Check for Art Basel in December, Ultra in March, Calle Ocho Festival in March, Miami Open tennis, and F1 Grand Prix in May. Year-round: Viernes Culturales on the last Friday of every month in Little Havana, Wynwood Art Walk on second Saturdays, and Lincoln Road Farmers Market every Sunday.

Caracas Bakery for Venezuelan pastries — the ham cachito is mandatory. Gramps Getaway just launched a breakfast pop-up at the marina. For a scene brunch, Rusty Pelican does bottomless mimosas with a skyline view. And any ventanita in Little Havana will get you a tostada and cafecito for under $5.

Miami doesn't close. E11EVEN is literally open 24/7 — the peak energy is 3-5am. Club Space goes until well past noon the next day. Mac's Club Deuce serves until 5am with cheap drinks. And plenty of ventanitas stay open late for a midnight croqueta and cafecito to keep the night going.

Start at Wynwood Walls for the outdoor murals, then just wander — the surrounding blocks have art on every surface. ICA Miami in the Design District is free and currently has the massive Dolce & Gabbana exhibition. PAMM on the waterfront is the contemporary art museum with killer bay views. And Vizcaya is a 1920s Italian villa with formal gardens that'll stop you in your tracks.

Twist on Washington Ave has been Miami's LGBTQ+ anchor for 25+ years — no cover, multiple rooms, dancing every night. Miami Beach Pride in April is one of the best in the country — the Ocean Drive parade with Art Deco hotels as backdrop is iconic. No. 3 Social in Wynwood does drag bingo on Sundays. Hotel Gaythering on Lincoln Road has nightly themed events.

Quick breakdown: South Beach is the beach/nightlife scene — touristy but iconic. Brickell is the urban/upscale core with rooftop bars and dining. Wynwood is street art and craft breweries. Little Havana is Cuban culture and salsa. Design District is luxury shopping and Michelin restaurants. Coral Gables is leafy, residential, and elegant. Coconut Grove is laid-back and artsy. Key Biscayne is where locals escape to real beaches.

text: Miami has an insane omakase scene. Shingo in Coral Gables is 14 seats and a Michelin star — maybe the best in the city. Hiden in Wynwood is hidden behind a taco stand and holds a star too. Ogawa in Little River flies fish from Toyosu Market. For a less intense experience, Makoto at Bal Harbour is excellent and easier to book.

text: La Mar by Gaston Acurio at the Mandarin Oriental is the gold standard — waterfront ceviche with Brickell Key views. For something more casual, Pisco y Nazca in Kendall does excellent lomo saltado and pisco sours. CVI.CHE 105 downtown is solid and always packed.

Little Haiti is one of Miami's most underrated neighborhoods. Chef Creole is the anchor — Haitian griot and conch salad under a thatched roof. Boia De nearby has a Michelin star hidden in a strip mall. The whole neighborhood is evolving fast with spots like La Natural and Ogawa putting it on the food map.

For the skyline view: Rusty Pelican on Key Biscayne, hands down. On the Miami River: Seaspice and Kiki on the River are scene-y. At the tip of South Beach: Smith & Wollensky. In Brickell: La Mar at the Mandarin Oriental. And Gramps Getaway at Rickenbacker Marina is the chill local move.

2026 is wild. Seia just opened on the 54th floor of Brickell — insane views and Italian food. Sunkissed in Brickell is doing late-night seafood. Sunny's Steakhouse in Little River went from pop-up to one of the hottest spots in America. Tequila Town is a 25,000 sq-ft agave experience in Hialeah. And Grotto Baths is bringing a social bathhouse to Wynwood.

Mac's Club Deuce on 14th Street has been pouring since 1964 — cash only, pool table, 2-for-1 happy hour that starts at 8 AM. Gramps in Wynwood has great pizza and actual air conditioning. Blackbird Ordinary in Brickell has a huge patio and strong cheap drinks. Jolene Soundroom is a Roaring Twenties basement turned dance floor.

Sugar at EAST Miami in Brickell is the rooftop king — Asian garden vibes with panoramic bay views. 1 Hotel South Beach rooftop has ocean views. Juvia on Lincoln Road has a stunning three-kitchen concept (Japanese-Peruvian-French) with skyline views. And if you can get into Seia on the 54th floor, nothing beats it.

Heat games at Kaseya Center downtown are electric — Heat Culture is real. Dolphins play at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, same spot as the F1 Grand Prix in May. Inter Miami is Messi's team — tickets are gold. Marlins at loanDepot Park in Little Havana is underrated: great food, retractable roof, cheap tickets.

Miami is surprisingly dog-friendly. Haulover Beach has an off-leash dog beach — north end, before the clothing-optional section. Hobie Beach on the Rickenbacker Causeway is another dog beach. Many restaurants have pet-friendly patios — Cerveceria La Tropical, Gramps, and most Wynwood spots. For boarding, check Dogma or WoofGang.
